claims.object_text: epilepsy, intellectual disability, and developmental delay
claims.quote: Natural variants to the GRIN1 gene, which encodes the obligatory GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor, are associated with severe neurological disorders that include epilepsy, intellectual disability, and developmental delay.
Here, we investigated the pathogenicity of three missense variants to the GRIN1 gene, p. Ile148Val (GluN1-3b[I481V]), p.Ala666Ser (GluN1-3b[A666S]), and p.Tyr668His (GluN1-3b[Y668H]).

claims.object_text: inhibited by ketamine and memantine with reduced potency; little effect on receptor function
claims.quote: Our data demonstrate that the GluN1(I481V) variant is inhibited by the open pore blockers ketamine and memantine with reduce potency but otherwise has little effect on receptor function.
By contrast, the other two variants exhibit gain-of-function molecular phenotypes.
Glycine sensitivity was enhanced in receptors containing the GluN1(A666S) variant

claims.object_text: reduced potency of memantine and ketamine; increased potency of MK-801 (A666S)
claims.quote: the potency of pore block by memantine and ketamine was reduced, whereas that for MK-801 was increased.
GluN1(Y668H)/2A receptors showed impaired surface expression

claims.object_text: increased sensitivity to glycine and glutamate by an order of magnitude (Y668H)
claims.quote: were more sensitive to glycine and glutamate by an order of magnitude

claims.object_text: impaired block by extracellular magnesium, memantine, ketamine, and MK-801 (Y668H)
claims.quote: and exhibited impaired block by extracellular magnesium ions, memantine, ketamine, and MK-801.

claims.object_text: activated by either glutamate or glycine alone (Y668H)
claims.quote: These variant receptors were also activated by either glutamate or glycine alone.

claims.object_text: opened to several conductance levels and activated more frequently (Y668H)
claims.quote: Single-receptor recordings revealed that this receptor variant opened to several conductance levels and activated more frequently than wild-type GluN1/2A receptors.

claims.object_text: GluN1[Y668] couples receptor gating to ion channel conductance; mutation may be associated with neurological disorder
claims.quote: Our study reveals a critical functional locus of the receptor (GluN1[Y668]) that couples receptor gating to ion channel conductance, which when mutated may be associated with neurological disorder.
